description: An introduction to the particle nature of matter and the mechanical properties of materials, including elasticity, plasticity, cohesion, adhesion, surface tension, capillarity, tension and Hooke's law.

mcq.questionText: All matter is made up of tiny particles called:
mcq.explanation: The basic particles of matter are atoms and molecules. Exam Tip: Cells are units of LIVING things. Matter is built from atoms and molecules.

mcq.questionText: The property of a material that allows it to return to its original shape after a stretching force is removed is called:
mcq.explanation: The ability to return to shape is elasticity. Exam Tip: Elastic materials (rubber, springs) return to shape; plastic materials stay deformed.

mcq.questionText: A material that does NOT return to its original shape after the force is removed is said to be:
mcq.explanation: A material that stays deformed is plastic. Exam Tip: Plasticine and wet clay are plastic; rubber is elastic.

mcq.questionText: The force of attraction between molecules of the SAME substance is called:
mcq.explanation: Attraction between like molecules is cohesion. Exam Tip: Cohesion = same substance (water-water); adhesion = different substances (water-glass).

mcq.questionText: The force of attraction between molecules of DIFFERENT substances is called:
mcq.explanation: Attraction between unlike molecules is adhesion. Exam Tip: Adhesion makes water wet glass and ink stick to paper.

mcq.questionText: The property by which the surface of a liquid behaves like a thin stretched skin is called:
mcq.explanation: The surface acting like a stretched skin is surface tension. Exam Tip: Surface tension lets insects walk on water and forms droplets into beads.

mcq.questionText: The rise or fall of a liquid in a narrow tube is called:
mcq.explanation: Liquid rising or falling in a narrow tube is capillarity. Exam Tip: Capillarity helps water rise in plant stems and oil rise in a lamp wick.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following materials is elastic?
mcq.explanation: A rubber band snaps back; clay, plasticine and gum stay deformed. Exam Tip: Rubber and springs are elastic.

mcq.questionText: When a spring is stretched by a force, the force that develops inside the spring opposing the stretch is called:
mcq.explanation: The internal pulling force is tension. Exam Tip: Tension is the pulling force in a stretched string, spring or rope.

mcq.questionText: According to Hooke's law, the extension of a spring is directly proportional to the:

options.text: Stretching force (load) applied, within the elastic limit

mcq.explanation: Extension is proportional to the load, provided the elastic limit is not exceeded. Exam Tip: Hooke's law: extension proportional to force (up to the elastic limit).

mcq.questionText: The maximum point up to which a material remains elastic is called the:
mcq.explanation: The maximum point is the elastic limit. Exam Tip: Past the elastic limit the material is permanently deformed.

mcq.questionText: Water rises up the stem of a plant mainly because of:
mcq.explanation: Capillary action, aided by adhesion, lifts water up the narrow tubes. Exam Tip: Capillarity in plants: water rises in the narrow tubes of the stem.

mcq.questionText: A steel needle can float on water without sinking because of:
mcq.explanation: The water surface acts like a skin (surface tension) supporting the light needle. Exam Tip: Surface tension supports small light objects even when denser than water.

mcq.questionText: Mercury in a narrow glass tube curves DOWNWARD in the middle (convex) because:

options.text: There is no force between molecules

mcq.explanation: In mercury, cohesion is stronger than adhesion, so it pulls together and curves down. Exam Tip: Water: adhesion > cohesion (curves up). Mercury: cohesion > adhesion (curves down).

mcq.questionText: Which state of matter has particles that are very close together and only vibrate in fixed positions?
mcq.explanation: In a solid, particles are tightly packed and vibrate in fixed positions. Exam Tip: Solid = tightly packed fixed; liquid = close but can move; gas = far apart.

fib.questionText: All matter is made up of tiny particles called atoms and ____.
fib.explanation: Atoms join to form molecules, and together they are the building blocks of all matter. Exam Tip: Atoms and molecules are the building blocks of all matter.

fib.questionText: The ability of a material to return to its original shape after the deforming force is removed is called ____.
fib.explanation: Returning to the original shape after the force is removed defines elasticity. Exam Tip: Rubber and springs show elasticity.

fib.questionText: The force of attraction between molecules of the same kind is called ____.
fib.explanation: Attraction between molecules of the same kind is cohesion. Exam Tip: Cohesion holds a water drop together.

fib.questionText: The force of attraction between molecules of different kinds is called ____.
fib.explanation: Attraction between molecules of different kinds is adhesion. Exam Tip: Adhesion makes water cling to glass.

fib.questionText: The property that makes the surface of a liquid behave like a stretched elastic skin is called ____.
fib.explanation: A liquid surface behaving like a stretched skin is surface tension. Exam Tip: Surface tension forms droplets and supports small insects.

fib.questionText: The rise or fall of a liquid in a very narrow tube is called ____.
fib.explanation: Rise or fall of a liquid in a very narrow tube is capillarity. Exam Tip: Capillarity draws oil up a lamp wick and water up plant stems.

fib.questionText: According to Hooke's law, extension is directly proportional to the applied force provided the ____ limit is not exceeded.
fib.explanation: Hooke's law holds only up to the elastic limit. Exam Tip: Beyond the elastic limit the spring is permanently stretched.

fib.questionText: The pulling force that develops in a stretched spring or string is called ____.
fib.explanation: The pulling force in a stretched spring or string is tension. Exam Tip: Tension acts along a stretched rope, string or spring.

fib.questionText: In water, ____ is greater than cohesion, so water wets glass and rises up the tube.
fib.explanation: Water wets glass and rises because adhesion is greater than cohesion. Exam Tip: Water: adhesion > cohesion (wets, rises). Mercury: cohesion > adhesion.

fib.questionText: A material such as plasticine that keeps its new shape after a force is removed is described as ____.
fib.explanation: A material that keeps its new shape is plastic. Exam Tip: Plastic materials do not spring back; elastic ones do.

tf.questionText: All matter is made up of tiny particles.
tf.explanation: Matter is built from atoms and molecules, so this is true. Exam Tip: The particle theory explains states of matter, diffusion and expansion.

tf.questionText: Elasticity is the ability of a material to return to its original shape after a force is removed.
tf.explanation: Returning to the original shape after the force is removed is exactly elasticity. Exam Tip: Rubber bands and springs are elastic.

tf.questionText: Cohesion is the attraction between molecules of different substances.
tf.explanation: Cohesion is between molecules of the same substance; attraction between different substances is adhesion. Exam Tip: Cohesion = same; adhesion = different. Swapped.

tf.questionText: Surface tension makes the surface of a liquid behave like a stretched skin.
tf.explanation: Surface tension makes the liquid surface act like a thin stretched skin. Exam Tip: Surface tension beads water into drops.

tf.questionText: Capillarity is the rise or fall of a liquid in a wide container.
tf.explanation: Capillarity occurs in a narrow tube, not a wide container. Exam Tip: Capillarity needs a NARROW tube; the narrower, the greater the rise.

tf.questionText: According to Hooke's law, doubling the load on a spring doubles its extension (within the elastic limit).
tf.explanation: Extension is proportional to load, so doubling the load doubles the extension within the elastic limit. Exam Tip: The proportional relationship holds only below the elastic limit.

tf.questionText: Beyond the elastic limit, a spring returns exactly to its original length.
tf.explanation: Past the elastic limit the spring is permanently deformed and does not fully return. Exam Tip: Beyond the elastic limit it is permanently deformed.

tf.questionText: Adhesion is the force that makes water stick to the surface of glass.
tf.explanation: Water sticking to glass is caused by adhesion between the different substances. Exam Tip: Adhesion (water-glass) makes water wet the glass.

tf.questionText: A rubber band is an example of a plastic material.
tf.explanation: A rubber band springs back, so it is elastic, not plastic. Exam Tip: Rubber = elastic; plasticine = plastic.

tf.questionText: Surface tension allows some small insects to move on the surface of water.
tf.explanation: Surface tension supports light insects on the water surface. Exam Tip: Pond-skaters walk on water thanks to surface tension.

summary.correctAnswer: The tiny particles from which all matter is made, atoms being the basic units and molecules being groups of joined atoms.
summary.explanation: The particle theory of matter is built on atoms and molecules. Exam Tip: Cells belong to living things; matter is made of atoms and molecules.

summary.correctAnswer: The ability of a material to return to its original shape after the deforming force is removed.
summary.explanation: Elastic materials store energy and spring back. Exam Tip: Rubber and springs are classic elastic materials.

summary.correctAnswer: The property of a material that keeps its new shape and does not return after the deforming force is removed.
summary.explanation: Plastic materials are permanently deformed by a force. Exam Tip: Plasticine and wet clay are plastic, not elastic.

summary.correctAnswer: The force of attraction between molecules of the same substance.
summary.explanation: Cohesion holds a liquid together, such as water to water. Exam Tip: Cohesion = same substance; do not confuse it with adhesion.

summary.correctAnswer: The force of attraction between molecules of different substances.
summary.explanation: Adhesion makes one substance cling to another. Exam Tip: Adhesion makes water wet glass and ink stick to paper.

summary.correctAnswer: The property by which the surface of a liquid behaves like a thin stretched elastic skin.
summary.explanation: Surface tension is caused by cohesion between surface molecules. Exam Tip: Surface tension forms droplets and supports small insects and needles.

summary.correctAnswer: The rise or fall of a liquid in a very narrow tube caused by adhesion and surface tension.
summary.explanation: Capillary rise is greater in narrower tubes. Exam Tip: Capillarity lifts water in plant stems and oil in a lamp wick.

summary.correctAnswer: The law stating that the extension of a spring is directly proportional to the applied force, provided the elastic limit is not exceeded.
summary.explanation: Doubling the load doubles the extension within the elastic limit. Exam Tip: Hooke's law only holds below the elastic limit.

summary.correctAnswer: The maximum point up to which a material remains elastic and can still return to its original shape.
summary.explanation: Beyond it the material is permanently deformed. Exam Tip: Past the elastic limit Hooke's law no longer applies.

summary.correctAnswer: The pulling force that develops inside a stretched spring, string or rope, opposing the stretch.
summary.explanation: Tension acts along the length of the stretched object. Exam Tip: Tension is a pulling force in a stretched string, spring or rope.

hoq.questionText: A spring is loaded: 0 N gives 0 cm, 2 N gives 1 cm, 4 N gives 2 cm, 6 N gives 3 cm. What does the pattern show, and what extension would 8 N most likely produce (within the elastic limit)?

options.text: Extension is proportional to load; 8 N gives 4 cm
Extension is random; 8 N gives 1 cm
Extension decreases with load; 8 N gives 0 cm
Extension is proportional to load; 8 N gives 8 cm

hoq.explanation: Each 2 N adds 1 cm, so extension = load / 2 (Hooke's law). For 8 N: 8 / 2 = 4 cm. Exam Tip: Look for a constant ratio (2 N per cm). Extend the pattern only WITHIN the elastic limit.

hoq.questionText: Water in a glass tube curves UPWARD at the edges (concave), while mercury curves DOWNWARD (convex). Explain using cohesion and adhesion.

options.text: For water, adhesion (water-glass) > cohesion, so it wets and rises; for mercury, cohesion > adhesion, so it does not wet and falls
Water has cohesion > adhesion; mercury has adhesion > cohesion

hoq.explanation: Water: adhesion to glass wins, so it climbs and curves up (wets). Mercury: cohesion wins, so it pulls in and curves down (does not wet). Exam Tip: Adhesion wins -> wets and curves UP (water). Cohesion wins -> curves DOWN (mercury). Option C reverses them.

hoq.questionText: Water rises higher in a very thin straw than in a wider one. A student links this to how water reaches the top of tall plants. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: The rise is due to capillarity, which is greater in narrower tubes; the same effect helps water rise in the fine tubes of plant stems
The rise is due to the weight of water, which is greater in narrow tubes
The rise is due to magnetism in the water
Narrow and wide tubes give the same rise

hoq.explanation: Capillary rise (adhesion + surface tension) is greater in narrower tubes; plant xylem tubes are very fine, so the same effect lifts water. Exam Tip: Capillary rise INCREASES as the tube gets narrower. Option B is the trap - water's weight opposes the rise.
